Aluminum foil Strains to be tested and containing fusions to β-lactamase (see Notes) Lysogeny Broth-Lennox (LB) media (see Recipes) PPBS plates (see Recipes) 10× phosphate buffer (see Recipes) Buffered saline (see Recipes) Ampicillin solution stocks (see Recipes) Lysogeny Broth-Lennox (LB) plates (see Recipes) Notes: We routinely use Salmonella typhimurium LT2, strain TH437 (S. typhimurium LT2 wild type) as a negative control (MIC 1.

and strain TH15737 (flgM-bla ΔflgHI fljBenxvh2 Δflk) as a positive control (MIC 100). These strains are available upon request. We insert the Bla fusion without its signal sequence (amino acids 24–286 of Bla) just before the stop codon of the gene of interest, in the chromosome, using the lambda red recombination technique. We routinely do not add linkers, but we see no reason they could not be added. Confirm that the DNA sequence of any construct made is correct and that the protein expression is unaffected by the fusion before conducting assays.

Recipes Ampicillin solution stocks For liquid assays: Prepare 10 mL stock solution of 100 mg/mL of ampicillin in water. Filter sterilize. Aliquot in 500 μL microcentrifuge tubes and keep at -20 °C until use. Use one single aliquot for each assay, to avoid freeze thawing. For PPBS-Ap plates: Prepare 100 mL stock solutions of 6 or 20 mg/mL of ampicillin in 50% ethanol/50% water, filter sterilize, and keep at -20 °C in the dark Notes: i. Ampicillin is sensitive to light; keep the antibiotic in the dark throughout all steps. ii. Prepare fresh stock solutions of sodium ampicillin every three months. Proteose peptone bile salt (PPBS) plates (1 L) Prepare Flasks A and B as follows: Flask A Flask B 17 g of Bacto peptone 3 g of Bacto proteose peptone 10 g of NaCl 1.5 g of Difco bile salt #3 500 mL of distilled water 12 g of agar 500 mL of distilled water Place media flasks in an autoclave-safe bin containing a small amount of water and autoclave for 30 min. Add the desired concentration of ampicillin solution to flask A as soon as the flasks can be hand touched (approximately 55 °C). Mix Flask A and B by pouring contents of flask A into B and then back and forth two more times, to ensure the liquid is well mixed. Pour plates. Protect plates from light. Place plates in plastic bags after two days of drying at room temperature. Place in a cardboard box to protect from light and store at 4 °C. Plates can be used for at least one month. Lysogeny LB plates (1 L) Prepare flasks A and B as follows: Flask A Flask B 10 g of tryptone 5 g of yeast extract 5 g of sodium chloride 12 g of agar 500 mL of distilled water 500 mL of distilled water Place media flasks in an autoclave-safe bin containing a small amount of water and autoclave for 30 min. Once the flasks can be hand touched (approximately 55 °C), mix Flask A and B by pouring contents of flask B into flask A and then back and forth two more times to ensure the liquid is well mixed. Pour plates. Place plates in plastic bags after two days of drying at room temperature. Store at 4 °C. Plates can be used for at least three months. Lysogeny LB media (1 L) Weigh the following ingredients and dissolve into 1,000 mL of distilled water: 10 g of tryptone 5 g of yeast extract 5 g of sodium chloride Aliquot into 200 mL bottles and autoclave for 30 min. Store autoclaved bottles at room temperature until use. 10× phosphate buffer (1 L) Weigh the following ingredients and dissolve into 500 mL of distilled water: 110 g of Na 2 HPO 4 ·7H 2 O 30 g of KH 2 PO 4 Adjust pH to 7 and add water up to 1 L. Sterilize by autoclaving. Buffered saline (1 L) Weigh the following ingredients and dissolve into 1,000 mL of distilled water: 8.5 g of sodium chloride 100 mL of 10× phosphate buffer Aliquot into 200 mL bottles and autoclave for 30 min. Store autoclaved bottles at room temperature until use.

steps.title: Validate β‑lactamase constructs
steps.instruction: Confirm DNA sequence of each chromosomal Bla‑fusion construct and verify that protein expression is unchanged before proceeding to the assay.

steps.title: Prepare overnight cultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate three independent single colonies of each bacterial strain (including a negative‑control strain lacking a β‑lactamase fusion) into 1 mL LB broth per tube and grow with aeration at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Dilute cultures 200‑fold
steps.instruction: Pipette 5 µL of each overnight culture into 995 µL of buffered saline; mix gently to obtain a 200‑fold dilution.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mg/mL ampicillin stock (Ap stock)
steps.instruction: Dissolve ampicillin sodium salt to 100 mg/mL in sterile water (10 mL total), filter‑sterilize, aliquot 500 µL into microcentrifuge tubes, store at –20 °C in the dark; prepare fresh every three months and protect from light.

steps.title: Create serial ampicillin dilutions for assay
steps.instruction: Generate an 11‑point dilution series (800 µg/mL to 0 µg/mL) in 50 mL conical tubes as follows:

substeps.instruction: Label tube 1 and add 50 mL LB broth.
Discard 400 µL of LB from tube 1 and add 400 µL of the 100 mg/mL Ap stock; mix – final concentration 800 µg/mL.
Label tubes 2–11; add 25 mL LB to each.
Transfer 25 mL from tube 1 into tube 2, vortex, then transfer 25 mL from tube 2 into tube 3, and continue sequentially through tube 10.
Tube 11 receives only LB (no ampicillin).
Resulting concentrations: 1 = 800 µg/mL, 2 = 400 µg/mL, 3 = 200 µg/mL, 4 = 100 µg/mL, 5 = 50 µg/mL, 6 = 25 µg/mL, 7 = 12.5 µg/mL, 8 = 6.25 µg/mL, 9 = 3.125 µg/mL, 10 = 1.565 µg/mL, 11 = 0 µg/mL.

steps.title: Load 96‑well plates with ampicillin and cells
steps.instruction: Dispense ampicillin solutions and diluted cells into the wells in the order described:

substeps.instruction: Determine the number of 96‑well plates required; number each plate and label sample wells (layout 12 × 8 as in Figure 1).
Using a 2000 µL electronic pipette repeater, add 198 µL of each ampicillin dilution to the appropriate wells, starting with tube 11 (no ampicillin) and proceeding to tube 1 (highest concentration).

Using a 20 µL electronic pipette repeater, add 2 µL of the 200‑fold diluted cell suspension to each well, beginning with the wells containing the lowest ampicillin concentration and ending with the highest.
Stack the plates, cap them, tape the stack together and to the shaker plate inside the incubator.
Wrap plates in aluminum foil (or keep in the dark) to protect ampicillin from light.

steps.title: Incubate assay plates
steps.instruction: Place the stacked plates in a shaking incubator set to 37 °C, 180 rpm, and incubate for 18 h.

steps.title: Prepare media and plate recipes
steps.instruction: Make all required solutions and agar plates before starting the assay:

substeps.instruction: Ampicillin solution stocks for liquid assays: 10 mL of 100 mg/mL ampicillin in water, filter‑sterilize, aliquot 500 µL, store at –20 °C in the dark (use one aliquot per assay).
Ampicillin stock for PPBS‑Ap plates: 100 mL of 6 mg/mL or 20 mg/mL ampicillin in 50 % ethanol/50 % water, filter‑sterilize, store at –20 °C in the dark.
PPBS agar plates (1 L total):
• Flask A – 17 g Bacto peptone, 10 g NaCl, 12 g agar, 500 mL distilled water.
• Flask B – 3 g Bacto proteose peptone, 1.5 g Difco bile salt #3, 500 mL distilled water.
• Autoclave both flasks together in a water‑filled bin for 30 min.
• Cool to ~55 °C, add the desired ampicillin concentration to Flask A, then mix by pouring the contents of Flask A into Flask B and back two more times.
• Pour the mixed medium into Petri dishes, protect from light, let plates dry for two days at room temperature, then place in plastic bags, store in a cardboard box at 4 °C, and use within one month.
LB agar plates (1 L total):
• Flask A – 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl, 12 g agar, 500 mL distilled water.
• Flask B – 5 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl, 500 mL distilled water.
• Autoclave both flasks together for 30 min.
• Cool to ~55 °C, mix by pouring Flask B into Flask A and back two more times.
• Pour plates, dry two days, store in plastic bags at 4 °C; plates remain usable for at least three months.
LB liquid media (1 L): dissolve 10 g tryptone, 5 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl in 1 L distilled water, aliquot into 200 mL bottles, autoclave 30 min, store at room temperature.
10× phosphate buffer (1 L): dissolve 110 g Na₂HPO₄·7H₂O and 30 g KH₂PO₄ in 500 mL water, adjust pH to 7.0, add water to 1 L, autoclave.
Buffered saline (1 L): dissolve 8.5 g NaCl in 1 L water, add 100 mL of the 10× phosphate buffer, aliquot into 200 mL bottles, autoclave 30 min, store at room temperature.
